items.title: Delegating Knowledge: Belief in AI Sufficiency and its Consequences for How People Process Information
items.abstract: Generative AI produces information on demand, raising the question of why one would ever learn something that a chatbot can always retrieve. In this paper, we introduce Belief in AI Sufficiency (BAS): the belief that acquiring and retaining knowledge is less valuable because AI can provide it when needed. BAS represents a qualitatively distinct conceptual domain from the Google effect, cognitive offloading, and the “News Finds Me” perception. Using four preregistered studies in the United States (development, N = 307; validation, N = 903; experiment, N = 767; test-retest, N = 298), we present evidence for a 12-item BAS measure with a strong general factor structure. In the validation survey, higher BAS was associated with greater reliance on heuristic and less systematic processing, and with reduced factual knowledge. In the experiment, BAS strongly predicted the likelihood to delegate a learning task to AI. The relationship between BAS and the gap between self-reported and measured knowledge was smaller, reflecting reduced accuracy rather than an illusion of knowledge. Finally, BAS scores were approximately equal in mean level and showed moderate rank-order stability across a 3-month period. BAS is one way to measure how far AI is becoming central to the study of how people learn.

items.abstract: Research Question (RQ): How has research on AI and workload developed over time, and what themes, methods, and gaps shape current understanding of workload and well-being in AI-enabled work? Purpose: The purpose of this study is to map and describe the research landscape on AI and workload, identifying key topics, publication trends, and gaps relevant to work design, management, and well-being. Method: The study applies bibliometric analysis to peer-reviewed publications indexed in Scopus over the last five years. A transparent search strategy covers AI, workload, and related concepts. The analysis examines publication growth, citation patterns, source and author networks, and keyword co-occurrence, supported by science-mapping techniques. Interpretation is guided by work-design and job demands perspectives. Results: We found strong growth in publications across the AI and workload cross-section and high interdisciplinarity of the field. We reveal dominant research themes, the concentration of research across regions, and methodological patterns, as well as areas that remain understudied in relation to AI, workload, and well-being. Organization: By synthesizing a fragmented body of research, the study helps managers and HR professionals understand where evidence on the use of AI is well-developed and where caution or further evaluation is needed when implementing AI in work processes. Society: Clarifying how workload is addressed in AI-related research contributes to responsible AI use, worker health, and fair work practices in increasingly automated environments. Originality: The study offers a focused bibliometric overview of AI-related workload research, bringing together interdisciplinary perspectives on work design, stress, and well-being that are often studied separately. Limitations / further research: Bibliometric findings depend on coverage of a single database and on search choices and do not provide causal evidence. Future research should combine bibliometric mapping with empirical and intervention studies across sectors and regions.

items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dental magnification devices provide measurable clinical and ergonomic benefits; however, their adoption among undergraduate dental students remains limited in many institutions. This study aimed to assess awareness, usage patterns, attitudes, perceived barriers, and educational preferences regarding dental magnification among students at the School of Dentistry, University of Jordan. METHODS: A cross-sectional questionnaire-based survey was conducted among 802 dental students at different educational levels, including preclinical third-year students, clinical undergraduate students in the fourth and fifth years, and postgraduate trainees. Associations between demographic and educational variables and magnification-related responses were analysed using the chi-square and Kruskal-Wallis tests. Statistical significance was established at p < 0.05. RESULTS: = 17.558, p = 0.002). Male students reported significantly greater magnification use than female students (22.0% vs. 12.6%, p < 0.001). Despite the low rate of clinical use, most respondents (80.4%) agreed that magnification improves clinical accuracy. Cost was identified as the most common barrier to use (78.3%). Attendance at continuing education courses related to magnification was lowest among interns (14.5%). Most participants (84.0%) supported earlier integration of magnification training into the dental curriculum, with third year identified as the preferred stage for introduction. CONCLUSIONS: A substantial gap exists between students' positive perceptions of dental magnification and its actual clinical use. Financial barriers and limited curricular integration appear to be the main obstacles to adoption. Earlier incorporation of structured magnification training within undergraduate dental education may improve student exposure and uptake.

items.title: DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A RAG-BASED AI AGENT FOR ROBO-ADVISORS
items.abstract: This study focuses on the design and implementation of an agentic system based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture for automated financial advisory services (Robo-Advisors, RA). The relevance of this study lies in the knowledge limitations of large language models (LLMs) in domain-specific areas, such as the financial sector, where factual errors can lead to direct financial losses and regulatory risks. Based on a literature review, the class of tasks for a modern Robo-Advisor platform suitable for RAG-based solutions has been identified. The purpose of this research is to develop a RAG agent architecture for a Robo-Advisor service and verify its functionality on a working prototype. Functional requirements for an RA module were established to track the behaviour of financial assets within a specific investment portfolio. An analysis was conducted on the tools used to implement typical interaction scenarios with a RAG system (data acquisition, text preprocessing, vectorisation, data normalisation, LLM interaction, etc.). A software architecture was designed in which agent functions (obtaining stock prices, analysing financial news, automated reports, user communication) are reflected in separate software modules. The system is divided into an asynchronous indexing circuit and a synchronous user interaction circuit. The agent's memory is implemented as hybrid storage, where a relational database serves as the source of truth, and the vector index is a fully recoverable derivative artifact. A method for re-ranking news search results using a normalised time-of-publication coefficient is proposed. User interaction is implemented as a chatbot for a messenger. Pilot operation confirmed that the system meets the established requirements; identified shortcomings and limitations of the agent are described, along with methods for their resolution. The results of this study can be used to integrate RAG agents into full-scale Robo-Advisor services.

items.title: Design for Cognitive Friction in Human-AI Interaction: A Student‑Centred AI Scaffold for Cognitive Resilience and Intellectual Agility
items.abstract: This exploratory, design-oriented pilot case study examines Erwin, a student-centred AI scaffold designed to augment students’ thinking in an interdisciplinary design innovation module. Unlike answer-giving chatbots, Erwin adopts a supportive-critic stance: it provides stage-aware, dialogic scaffolding that widens idea spaces and supports criteria-based consolidation through nudges and commitments. The analysis drew on 1,999 student and Erwin turns organised into 171 sessions nested within 78 student logs, alongside post-module qualitative feedback. The study combined reflexive thematic analysis with a full-corpus, non-inferential descriptive analysis of selected interaction-process indicators, including initiative balance, futures probes, completed repair sequences, and system boundary or refusal episodes. A purposive sample of six final artefacts provided illustrative triangulation of interaction patterns and student project trajectories. The analysis identified four practices: disciplined divergence, in which Deliberate Cognitive Friction (DCF) prompts appeared alongside expanded frames without displacing agency; criteria-aware convergence, in which students translated broadened views into clearer problem statements, constraints, and next steps; cognitive resilience visible through repair and persistence sequences; and a supportive-critic experience shaped by answer resistance and meta-reflection. As this was a single-course pilot with no control condition, the descriptive indicators characterise observed interaction processes and contextualise the qualitative interpretation; they are not estimates of causal effects or direct measures of learning outcomes. Across cases, these practices appeared alongside traces of broadened ideation, criteria-guided consolidation, and futures-oriented reasoning in the illustrative artefact sample. The paper contributes situated empirical evidence for studying AI as human augmentation rather than substitution; a transferable design blueprint that operationalises DCF at the prompt policy layer through explainable prompts, resilience guardrails, and instrumentation for scaffolding-oriented LLM systems; and a process-oriented operationalisation of cognitive resilience for Human Computer Interaction in education, understood as interactional evidence of repair, persistence, and flexible reframing rather than as a demonstrated learning effect. The discussion offers implications for designing resilient, trust-preserving human-AI ecosystems that balance augmentation against risks of overreliance and cognitive offloading.

items.title: Design-Driven AI Integration in Education: A Human-Centered Approach
items.abstract: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in education is fundamentally transforming pedagogical practices, learning environments, and the roles of teachers and learners. While AI-driven systems offer considerable potential for personalization, efficiency, and data-informed decision-making, their educational value depends on how they are pedagogically framed, critically implemented, and ethically embedded within learning processes. This chapter argues that design thinking provides a robust, human-centered framework for aligning AI innovation with pedagogical goals, learner needs, and ethical considerations. Drawing on interdisciplinary perspectives from educational research, human-centered design, and AI studies, the chapter conceptualizes design thinking as a methodological and pedagogical bridge between technological advancement and meaningful learning design. It demonstrates how key design thinking principles—such as empathy, problem framing, iterative prototyping, and reflective evaluation—can guide the development of AI-enhanced learning environments. Building on this foundation, the chapter introduces a design-driven model for AI integration in education and illustrates its application in practice. It further examines implications for teaching and professional development, emphasizing a shift from tool-centered adoption toward competence-oriented, reflective, and ethically grounded pedagogical design. By positioning design thinking as a strategic framework for the responsible and human-centered integration of AI, the chapter contributes to current debates on rethinking pedagogy in the digital age and offers a structured approach to designing future-oriented learning environments.

items.title: Designing AI-Ready Teachers: Integrating Design Thinking into Contemporary Teacher Education
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into educational settings requires a fundamental reconsideration of how teachers are prepared for practice. This chapter argues that design thinking, an iterative, human-centered methodology for problem-solving and innovation, offers a particularly productive framework for reshaping teacher education so that graduates are equipped not merely to use AI tools but also to evaluate them critically, adapt them pedagogically, and deploy them ethically. Drawing on scholarship in design thinking, teacher professional learning, AI in education, and technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK), the chapter maps the conceptual and practical terrain of AI-ready teacher preparation. It examines the current state of teacher education, identifies persistent gaps in preparing educators for AI-infused classrooms, and proposes an integrated Design Thinking for AI-Ready Teaching (DT-ART) model. The chapter concludes with implications for curriculum designers, teacher educators, and institutional policymakers navigating the digital transformation of schooling.

items.title: Designing Sustainable Science Learning for Adolescents through Design Thinking, Artificial Intelligence, and Short-Form Media
items.abstract: The explosive rise of short-form videos (SFVs), commonly exemplified by social media reels, has significantly reshaped adolescents’ attention patterns, driven by neurocognitive mechanisms such as novelty seeking, rapid feedback, and dopaminergic reward cycles. While these mechanisms are often associated with distraction, compulsive media use, and reduced sustained attention in teenagers, they also reveal untapped potential for educational design constraining ethically and pedagogically. This chapter proposes a conceptual framework that integrates Design Thinking (DT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to repurpose the engagement affordances of SFVs for the development of sustainable science learning among adolescents. Within the framework, SFVs function as controlled attention-entry triggers that introduce real-world scientific phenomena in brief, engaging formats tailored to adolescent cognitive styles. Design Thinking structures learner engagement into finite, reflective inquiry cycles, supporting agency and problem-solving, two key developmental needs during adolescence. AI operates as an adaptive orchestration layer, supporting personalized pacing, cognitive load regulation, and formative feedback, while intentionally avoiding the addictive dynamics typical of commercial media platforms. By re-engineering short-form engagement within structured pedagogical loops, the framework transforms momentary attention capture into disciplined scientific inquiry, systems-oriented reasoning, and durable conceptual understanding. This chapter contributes to emerging discussions on attention-aware pedagogy for youth, offering a theoretically grounded approach to align digital engagement mechanisms with the long-term sustainability of science learning processes for adolescent learners.

items.title: Determinan Keluhan Tendinitis Pada Pekerja Manual Handling : Determinants of Tendinitis Complaints Among Manual Handling Workers
items.abstract: Tendinitis merupakan salah satu gangguan musculoskeletal disorders yang ditandai dengan terjadi peradangan pada tendon, yaitu jaringan ikat kuat yang menghubungkan otot ke tulang. Kondisi ini biasanya disebabkan oleh penggunaan otot secara berlebihan, cedera, atau kondisi rematik lainnya. Aktivitas manual handling merupakan salah satu pekerjaan yang memiliki risiko terhadap gangguan muskuloskeletal, termasuk tendinitis. Gerakan mengangkat, membawa, menarik, dan memindahkan beban yang dilakukan secara berulang dapat memberikan beban berlebih pada jaringan otot dan tendon. Gudang Beras Bulog Cabang Gorontalo merupakan salah satu tempat kerja yang masih mengandalkan aktivitas manual handling dalam berbagai proses distribusinya. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis faktor-faktor yang berhubungan dengan keluhan tendinisi pada buruh yang melakukan aktivitas manual handling di pabrik beras perum bulog cabang Gorontalo. Penelitian ini menggunakan metotode penelitian kuantitatif dengan jenis penelitian analitik observasional dan desain cross-sectional. Populasi dan Sampel dalam penelitian ini berjumlah 50 buruh angkut teknik pengambilan sampel adalah total sampling. Variable yang akan diteliti adalah masa kerja, kebiasaan merokok dan frekuensi angkat. Uji statistik yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini adalah uji Spearman Rank. Hasil analisis menggunakan uji Spearman Rank menunjukkan bahwa ada hubungan yang signifikan antara kebiasaan merokok (p = 0,003; r = 0,413), masa kerja (p = 0,001; r = 0,469, dan frekuensi angkat (p = 0,008; r = 0,373) dengan keluhan tendinitis. Kesimpulan bahwa kebiasaan merokok, masa kerja dan frekuensi angkat berhubungan signifikan dengan keluhan tendinitis. Disarankan adanya intervensi ergonomis dan pelatihan mengenai postur kerja yang benar sebagai upaya pencegahan terjadinya keluhan tendinitis pada buruh angkut. Tendinitis is one of the musculoskeletal disorders characterized by inflammation of the tendon, a strong connective tissue that connects muscles to bones. This condition is commonly caused by overuse of the muscles, injury, or other rheumatic conditions. Manual handling activities are among the occupational tasks that pose a risk of musculoskeletal disorders, including tendinitis. Repetitive lifting, carrying, pulling, and moving of loads can place excessive stress on muscles and tendons. The Bulog Rice Warehouse, Gorontalo Branch, is a workplace that still relies heavily on manual handling activities in various distribution processes. This study aimed to analyze the factors associated with tendinitis complaints among workers performing manual handling activities at the Perum BULOG Rice Factory, Gorontalo Branch. This quantitative study employed an observational analytic design with a cross-sectional approach. The study population and sample consisted of 50 manual material-handling workers, selected using a total sampling technique. The variables examined were smoking habits, length of employment, and lifting frequency. Statistical analysis was performed using the Spearman rank correlation test. The results showed significant associations between smoking habits (p = 0.003; r = 0.413), length of employment (p = 0.001; r = 0.469), and lifting frequency (p = 0.008; r = 0.373) and tendinitis complaints. In conclusion, smoking habits, length of employment, and lifting frequency were significantly associated with tendinitis complaints among manual handling workers. Ergonomic interventions and training on proper working postures are recommended as preventive measures to reduce the occurrence of tendinitis complaints among manual handling workers.

items.title: Determining key approaches to enhancing the survivability of armored vehicle crews, considering the use of situational awareness systems in modern warfare
items.abstract: The study aims to provide a theoretical rationale for key approaches to enhancing the survivability of armored vehicle crews–incorporating situational awareness systems–and to develop a novel method for assessing the extent to which these systems contribute to the crew's defensive response. The methodological framework combines systems, structural-functional, comparative, and criteria-based approaches, alongside a content analysis of scholarly works, the decomposition of the situational awareness cycle, and a custom point-based assessment method. Crew survivability is viewed as the outcome of the coordinated operation of systems for observation, threat detection, identification and prioritization, information exchange, decision support, protection, and the restoration of control following adverse impacts. It is established that situational awareness serves a preventive function within the survivability system of armored vehicles, as it shifts the initiation of the defensive response to a stage preceding the actual impact. A six-criterion assessment system is proposed, covering the continuity and completeness of observation, timeliness of detection, resilience of information support, quality of prioritization, integration of information exchange, and the capacity to sustain the crew's defensive response. A 0–4 point scale and an integral index are used to compare the conceptual approaches. The scientific novelty lies in interpreting situational awareness as a functional component of ensuring crew survival through preventive measures and in formulating the "perception–recognition–assessment–decision–protective reaction" sequence as an object of theoretical evaluation. The practical significance of the results stems from their potential application in substantiating modernization directions for armored weaponry and equipment, preliminarily comparing information support options, and establishing development priorities for situational awareness systems.

items.title: Developing an AI Governance Readiness Index (AIGRI) for Indian Higher Education Institutions
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming higher education with intelligent learning systems, automated administration, research support, academic assessment, and institutional decision-making. As Indian Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) increasingly incorporate AI-enabled technologies, the lack of a standardized framework for evaluating institutional readiness for responsible AI governance has become a significant policy and administrative challenge. Current evaluation mechanisms primarily emphasize digital infrastructure and technology adoption, neglecting critical aspects such as ethical governance, institutional policy, regulatory compliance, data governance, academic integrity, human capacity development, and transparency, accountability, and risk management. In this paper, we propose developing an AI Governance Readiness Index (AIGRI) as a multidimensional framework to evaluate the preparedness of Indian Higher Education Institutions for the responsible and sustainable adoption of AI. The proposed index is structured around eight interconnected dimensions: Institutional Leadership and Governance, AI Policy and Regulatory Compliance, Digital Infrastructure, Data Governance and Cybersecurity, Human Capacity and AI Literacy, Ethical and Responsible AI Practices, Academic and Research Integrity, and Continuous Evaluation and Innovation. Each dimension is associated with measurable indicators that enable institutions to assess their current status, identify governance gaps, and formulate evidence-based strategies for improvement. The study employs a qualitative doctrinal and policy research approach, underpinned by an extensive review of national education policies, AI governance frameworks, international ethical AI guidelines, and literature on higher education quality assurance. The paper proposes a preliminary scoring model based on principles of responsible AI, good governance, and institutional accountability, which can then be validated through empirical research with universities across India. The proposed AIGRI is a practical governance tool for university administrators, policymakers, accreditation agencies, and regulatory bodies to assess AI readiness systematically. It also contributes to the emerging discourse of AI governance by shifting the focus from technology adoption to institutional preparedness, ethical implementation, and governance maturity. The framework could be a valuable addition to national quality assurance efforts, such as NAAC. It could be aligned with India’s vision of digitally empowered, globally competitive, and socially responsible higher education institutions. The study concludes that the development of a standardized AI Governance Readiness Index can guide policy decisions, enhance institutional resilience, encourage responsible AI adoption, and aid sustainable transformation of higher education in the era of intelligent technologies.

items.title: Developing Middle School Students’ Interest in Physical Education: A Pedagogical Model and Experimental Results
items.abstract: Fostering sustained interest in physical education among middle school students is regarded as an important factor in improving the effectiveness of school physical education within the framework of the updated educational content in the Republic of Kazakhstan. At the same time, declining student motivation highlights the need for pedagogical approaches that can enhance students’ engagement in the educational process. The purpose of this study was to develop and experimentally evaluate a pedagogical model aimed at fostering middle school students’ interest in physical education. The study was conducted at Kanysh Satpayev Gymnasium in Karaganda, Kazakhstan, and involved students from Grades 6B and 6G. The research methods included a review of the scientific literature, a questionnaire survey, pedagogical observation, physical fitness testing, a pedagogical experiment, and statistical analysis. The proposed pedagogical model was based on the integrated use of game-based, interactive, and digital educational technologies designed to enhance students’ cognitive engagement and personal interest in physical education. The experimental results demonstrated a positive change in students’ level of interest in physical education: the proportion of students with a high level of interest increased from 22.39% to 44.48%, whereas the proportion of students with a low level of interest decreased from 27.22% to 15.16%. In addition, improvements in the physical fitness of students in the experimental group were observed. The findings provide evidence supporting the effectiveness of the proposed pedagogical model and suggest its potential applicability to the organization of physical education in general secondary schools in the Republic of Kazakhstan.

items.title: DEVELOPING THE PROFESSIONAL IDENTITY OF HIGH SCHOOL ESL TEACHERS IN HO CHI MINH CITY UNDER VIETNAM’S 2018 GENERAL EDUCATION CURRICULUM
items.abstract: ABSTRACTThis study provides a systematic review of the conceptual foundations of language teachers’ professional identity, using a dialogical approach and an integrative perspective that incorporates personal, contextual, and professional factors. It also describes the current state of professional identity development among upper-secondary teachers teaching English as a second language in Ho Chi Minh City and examines perceived influencing factors. Data collection was performed via Google Form, with a survey administered to 182 teachers working in upper-secondary schools in Ho Chi Minh City. Descriptive statistical data analysis reveals that the overall professional identity index stands at a relatively high level. Dimensions related to professional commitment and pedagogical valyes score highly, whereas teacher agency and adaptability to curriculum and assessment changes are generally lower. Among the constraining factors are assessment workload, examination pressure, and administrative duties, which are rated as having the strongest impact. On the other hand, facilitating factors include intrinsic motivation, collegial collaboration, and feedback on students’ learning progress. On this basis, the article proposes recommendations at the three levels, i.e. individual, school, and system levels, to support sustainable professional identity development in the context of implementing the 2018 General Education Curriculum.

items.title: Development and expert evaluation of a culturally adapted large language model for Malay clinical history-taking simulation: mixed methods study
items.abstract: Background Clinical history-taking is a core medical competency, but conventional teaching may be limited by patient availability, variable clinical exposure, and restricted opportunities for repeated practice. Large language models (LLMs) may support simulated practice; however, their clinical, linguistic, and cultural suitability requires careful evaluation in multilingual settings. Objective This study aimed to develop and expert-evaluate a culturally and linguistically adapted English–Malay clinical dialogue corpus and to descriptively benchmark a fine-tuned LLM framework for clinical history-taking simulation in Malaysian undergraduate medical education. Methods A multiphase mixed-methods development and evaluation study was conducted across nine internal medicine systems. Of 63,250 AI-generated dialogue entries, each comprising a simulated doctor inquiry and corresponding patient response, 59,184 (93.6%) underwent consultant-level subject matter expert review using an author-developed holistic 5-point rubric informed by clinical relevance, accuracy, clarity and coherence, completeness, and human-likeness. Free-text comments were analysed inductively. After SME evaluation and clinical-quality and mechanical filtering, 58,886 entries across 2,497 simulated patient profiles were retained. The profiles were partitioned into 1,997 training profiles, 250 validation profiles, and 250 held-out test profiles. Four model configurations were descriptively benchmarked using the same held-out profiles and an automated large language model judge. This benchmark was intended for internal model comparison and did not constitute independent external or human clinical validation of the post-fine-tuning model outputs. Results Mean subject matter expert scores were 4.52/5 for simulated doctor inquiries and 4.58/5 for simulated patient responses. Qualitative analysis identified recurring limitations involving question structure, incomplete probing, repetition, linguistic accuracy, over-explanation, and simulated-patient realism. In descriptive benchmarking, the fine-tuned model achieved the highest observed mean score among the four configurations evaluated. Conclusions Developing a consultant-reviewed, culturally adapted English–Malay clinical dialogue corpus and using it to fine-tune an LLM for simulated history-taking was feasible. The fine-tuned model achieved the highest observed score in the internal automated benchmark, but this finding does not establish statistical, clinical, or educational superiority. The post-fine-tuning model outputs were not independently evaluated by clinicians in the present study. The framework may offer a scalable, contextually relevant supplement to clinical communication training, but blinded human evaluation of post-fine-tuning outputs, targeted safety assessment, external validation, and learner-outcome evaluation are required before routine student-facing implementation.

items.title: Development and field evaluation of a UAV-based supervision framework for ropeaccess operations in rockfall mitigation projects
items.abstract: Rockfall mitigation projects involve high occupational health and safety (OHS) risks due to steep topography, hardto-access work zones, rope-access operations, and environmental uncertainties. In such projects, conventional supervision and communication practices may be limited by blind spots, restricted visibility, and difficult terrain conditions. This study develops and field-evaluates an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based supervision framework to support OHS planning and operational coordination in rope-access operations carried out within rockfall mitigation projects. A descriptive and exploratory field-based research design was adopted. Questionnaire data were collected from 128 Rope Access Technicians (RATs) working in 16 active rockfall mitigation projects in different regions of Türkiye. The survey examined participants’ professional profiles, accident experiences, safety checks, communication and supervision practices, UAV awareness, UAV-related training status, and perceptions regarding UAV-supported monitoring. Field observations were also used to document the physical and operational characteristics of rope-access worksites. Based on the survey findings and field observations, a UAV-based supervision framework was structured around real-time visual monitoring, blind-spot reduction, communication support, hazard observation, and operational coordination. The proposed framework was then examined through a single-site pilot implementation in an active rockfall mitigation project. The findings indicate that RATs generally perceive UAV-supported monitoring and communication as potentially useful for improving situational awareness and supporting field coordination. The pilot implementation provided observational evidence that UAVs can assist supervisors by extending visual access to hardto-observe work areas. However, the study does not claim to demonstrate quantitative reductions in accident rates, work duration, or costs. The proposed UAV-based framework should therefore be considered a complementary decision-support and supervision tool rather than a replacement for trained rope-access supervision.

items.title: Development and Validation of the Occupational Safety Awareness Scale for Motorcycle Couriers
items.abstract: Motorcycle couriers in the platform-based gig economy are exposed to substantial occupational risks, yet no validated instrument exists to measure their occupational health and safety (OHS) awareness. This study develops and validates the Occupational Safety Awareness Scale for Motorcycle Couriers (OSAS-MC) to address this gap. Drawing on Türkiye’s OHS Law No. 6331, international OHS standards, and feedback from five domain experts, an initial item pool was generated and refined into a 30-item, six-dimensional instrument covering OHS Legislation Knowledge, OHS Practices, Personal Protective Equipment Use, Motorbike Use, OHS Exposure, and OHS Risk Factors. The scale was administered to 265 actively employed motorcycle couriers in Türkiye. Exploratory factor analysis supported a six-factor solution explaining 67.79% of the variance, and confirmatory factor analysis indicated an acceptable model fit (CFI = 0.875; RMSEA = 0.076; χ²/df = 2.543). Internal consistency was high overall (Cronbach’s α = 0.878) and across sub-dimensions (α = 0.805–0.895), and item discrimination was confirmed via upper-lower 27% group comparisons. The OSAS-MC offers a reliable, context-sensitive instrument for assessing safety awareness in high-risk, platform-mediated delivery work, and provides policymakers, platform operators, and labour organisations with a diagnostic tool to identify awareness gaps and guide targeted interventions.

items.title: DEVELOPMENT OF A CONCEPTUAL MODEL OF COMMUNICATION FACTORS IN DISTRIBUTED PROJECT MANAGEMENT
items.abstract: Communication management in distributed projects remains a critical scientific challenge driven by the spatial and organizational dispersion of teams, cultural and language barriers, and the lack of formalized models for systematizing communication factors in the context of digital transformation. This study aims to develop a conceptual model of communication factors in distributed project management, with a focus on environmental projects. The research object is the communication processes between stakeholders in distributed projects. The theoretical foundation rests on active systems theory, systems analysis, and leading project management standards (PMBoK, ISO 21500:2021, GreenPM). The study applies a two-level systems analysis framework: the operational level captures direct information exchange between stakeholders through the sender–message–channel–receiver–feedback model, while the managerial level addresses purposeful regulation of communications within a project. The proposed conceptual model identifies each stakeholder as an active system defined by a seven-parameter tuple: composition, structure, participation timeline, objective function, admissible strategy sets, functioning order, and participant awareness. The model formalizes the impact of both controlled and uncontrolled factors on stakeholder states as senders and receivers of information, systematizing the influence of technological, organizational, and human factors on the effectiveness of project participant interaction. Four types of informational uncertainty are distinguished: interval, probabilistic, fuzzy, and mixed. The model encompasses six communication management subsystems, ranging from stakeholder identification to collaboration effectiveness assessment. The practical value of the findings lies in establishing a methodological basis for optimizing communication strategies in distributed projects, reducing information asymmetry, minimizing communication risks under conditions of spatial and organizational dispersion, with a focus on environmental projects as an example of complex, multi-stakeholder distributed initiatives.

items.title: DEVELOPMENT OF A DIGITAL HUMAN MODEL FOR SIMULATION-BASED ERGONOMIC POSTURAL FIT ASSESSMENT OF SPECIALIZED VEHICLE DRIVERS
items.abstract: This study develops a digital human model (DHM) for ergonomic assessment of specialized vehicle drivers. The study was conducted on 278 Vietnamese adults, consisting of 139 individuals aged 20–29 years and 139 aged 30–39 years. Human body shape was reconstructed from two RGB images acquired from frontal and lateral views using a deep-learning-based approach implemented in the open-source SMPL-X framework. The reconstructed 3D models were used to derive key anthropometric parameters for evaluating driver postural fit during vehicle operation. A digital model of the KAMAZ-6560 cabin was developed from 3D-scanned vehicle data to accurately represent the actual cabin geometry and major interior components. Based on the synthesized anthropometric data, three representative body-size models corresponding to the lower, median, and upper anthropometric dimensions were selected. These models were integrated into Siemens NX using the JACK digital human modeling environment to simulate driving postures. Driver postural fit was evaluated according to the ergonomic joint-angle criteria proposed by Porter, with particular attention to the positions of the steering wheel, clutch pedal, and driver's seat. The results provide a digital human modeling framework for population-specific ergonomic assessment and support the ergonomic design and optimization of specialized vehicle cabins.

items.title: Development of An English Language Learning Model Through Gamification Technology for Higher Education
items.abstract: This study investigated higher education instructors' needs regarding gamified English language learning and developed an Applied Linguistics-informed instructional model for English as a Foreign Language (EFL) instruction. Grounded in Second Language Acquisition (SLA) theory—including Gardner's (1985) motivation framework, Communicative Language Teaching (CLT) principles, and Self-Determination Theory (SDT)—the study employed an Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation (ADDIE)-guided Design and Development Research (DDR) approach. A purposive sample of 158 EFL instructors completed a validated 15-item questionnaire (IOC = 0.80–1.00; α = 0.81). Findings indicated strong support for gamification in promoting communicative engagement, learner autonomy, and intrinsic motivation. Based on these findings, a five-component gamification-integrated model was developed and evaluated by five experts using an 11-item instrument (α = 0.85), achieving an overall mean rating of 4.60 (very high). The study contributes to Applied Linguistics and English language education by presenting an SLA-informed model that operationalizes gamification as a structured communicative pedagogy rather than isolated game mechanics, offering an empirically informed and theoretically grounded framework for EFL instruction in Thai higher education.

items.title: Developments in the Field of Photography and the Integration of Artificial Intelligence and Smart Technologies in a Developed India
items.abstract: Abstract Developments in the field of photography and the contribution of artificial intelligence have been remarkable in a developing India. The journey from early optical and chemical processes to digital visual communication has been significant. Technologies ranging from everyday applications to film, digital photography, smart photography, cloud platforms, machine learning, generative AI, drones, and IoT devices (such as Alexa) have vastly expanded the possibilities for capturing, processing, interpreting, and sharing images. Modern photography is no longer limited to just cameras, lenses, digital sensors, and photographers; smart technologies are increasingly playing a pivotal role in processes such as focusing, exposure, color correction, noise reduction, dynamic range enhancement, subject recognition, image segmentation, autofocus, image enhancement, and post-production. Research into AI and photography indicates that machine learning and computational processing have transformed the traditional boundaries between image capture and image processing. In India, these changes are unfolding within a digital framework. The Government of India’s 'IndiaAI' mission received approval in March 2024, aiming to strengthen computing infrastructure, data availability, AI innovation, and world-class development. This emerging technology ecosystem directly impacts photography and visual media education, as well as professional fields such as journalism, advertising, fashion product imaging, scientific documentation, wildlife and heritage conservation, and the creative industries. Furthermore, generative AI is driving a profound transformation; images can now be enhanced, recreated, modified, or generated from scratch without every visible element being directly linked to an optical phenomenon. This opens up new creative opportunities. However, issues regarding authenticity, the author's copyright, privacy, consent, employment, cultural representation, and public trust also arise. This research paper examines the historical evolution of photography, the opportunities for India in the field of photography alongside smart technology, the challenges faced by photographers and educators, and a proposed framework for responsible photography in a developing India.

items.title: Diagnostic Performance of Artificial Intelligence for Proximal Caries Detection on Bitewing Radiographs: A Systematic Review and Diagnostic Test Accuracy Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To systematically evaluate the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI) systems for detecting proximal caries lesions on bitewing radiographs. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Electronic searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between January 2000 and March 2026. Studies evaluating AI-based systems for proximal caries detection on bitewing radiographs were included. True-positive, false-positive, true-negative, and false-negative values were extracted directly or reconstructed from reported diagnostic accuracy metrics when sufficient information was available. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were estimated separately using random-effects models on the logit scale. RESULTS: Eleven studies were included in the qualitative synthesis, of which three studies provided sufficient 2×2 contingency table data for quantitative synthesis. The pooled sensitivity and specificity of AI systems for proximal caries detection were 0.73 (95% CI 0.70–0.75) and 0.92 (95% CI 0.69–0.99), respectively. Most included studies demonstrated promising diagnostic performance using deep learning architectures, particularly convolutional neural networks and YOLO-based models. CONCLUSION: AI systems demonstrated promising diagnostic performance for detecting proximal caries lesions on bitewing radiographs. However, methodological heterogeneity and limited external validation remain important limitations. Further prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm the clinical applicability of AI-assisted caries detection systems.

items.title: Diagnóstico general del uso de la inteligencia artificial en el sector público de México
items.abstract: The objective of this research is to identify, characterize, and analyze artificial intelligence (AI) applications used in the Mexican public sector. A quantitative methodology using descriptive statistics was used. The analysis shows that the use of AI in the Mexican public sector is concentrated in the Executive Branch and in sectors related to security, justice, government, economy, finance, and transparency. This technology is primarily used to improve communication with citizens and to increase organizational efficiency, employing natural language processing and machine learning to perform interaction tasks through chatbots and in image, voice, and text recognition tasks. The use of AI in the Mexican public sector presents marked institutional, territorial, sectoral, and functional asymmetries. It also reflects a strong technological dependence on the private sector and the need to strengthen internal capacities.

items.title: dialogue.txt: a standing, talk-only consent to be contacted (specification, draft 1.0)
items.abstract: AI systems that research a topic rely on what is published on the web. Much useful knowledge is not published. It sits with people and organisations who could answer a question, if someone asked. dialogue.txt is a small, machine-readable file on a website (/.well-known/dialogue.txt). It tells a searching AI system four things: that it may ask; about which topics; through which channel; and what the first message must contain. The first message only proposes a bridge. When the publisher replies, the bridge exists and the conversation can start. The file permits talk, never action. An example. An AI system researches traffic flow. A navigation company's dialogue.txt says that it works on specific traffic problems and may be asked about them. Without the file, the system can at best report that the company exists. If the solution is not public, it is missed. With the file, the system can ask. This record contains the specification, the field registry, a fill-in template, examples, a validator, a local try-it page, the test summary (five language models from five providers, more than 3,500 recorded model calls) and the Internet-Draft draft-wolf-dialogue-txt-00. About the author. Dimitri Wolf is an engineer. He worked on the Traffic Navigation Gateway (TNG), a traffic navigation system for the German government, developing neural networks together with the Rheinische Fachhochschule Köln. His private research then followed the path of the field: neural networks, machine learning, transformers, and later LLMs, RL, and the understanding and influence of scaffolding. dialogue.txt is a private research project, not his job and not a product. The ideas behind it grew over about ten years of this research. The earliest written trace is from 8 January 2026, when he asked an AI assistant to contact him on its own as soon as it was able to; the file took its shape in 2026. items.title: Differentiation of Family Values: A Quantitative Research on Socio-Demographic Determinants
items.abstract: This study examines the extent to which family values vary according to socio-demographic determinants -gender, age, educational attainment, occupational status, and mode of spouse acquaintance. Data were collected from 287 parents of primary school- age children in Düzce, Turkey, using the Family Values Scale, and analyzed through independent-samples t tests and one-way ANOVA. The findings indicate that women attach greater significance to the mother–child relationship and participatory decision-making, whereas men emphasize kinship ties, childrearing, marriage, spousal loyalty, and the economic functions of the family, reflecting more traditional orientations. Self-initiated marriages were associated with stronger emotional bonds. Younger respondents expressed more liberal attitudes toward sexuality and unconventional values, middle-aged participants prioritized democratic decision-making, and older participants showed stronger adherence to marital commitment and loyalty. Education was a critical factor: lower schooling levels corresponded to greater endorsement of traditional norms, and higher levels to more egalitarian orientations. Occupationally, health professionals held more liberal perspectives, while housewives and private-sector employees showed stronger traditional attachments. Overall, family values in Turkey appear shaped simultaneously by socio-demographic characteristics and the interplay between tradition and modernity, underscoring the relevance of policies promoting education, gender equality, and labor force participation

items.title: Digital Competence of Preservice Primary School Teachers: The Role of Digital Material Development Experience and Self-Assessed Artificial Intelligence Use Competence
items.abstract: This study aimed to determine the digital competence levels of preservice primary school teachers, examine whether their competence differed according to personal and experiential variables, and investigate the relationship between self-assessed artificial intelligence (AI) use competence and digital competence. The study employed descriptive and correlational survey designs with 119 preservice teachers enrolled in primary school teacher education programs at five universities. Data were collected through a Personal Information Form, which included a single-item self-assessment of AI use competence, and the 25-item, five-dimensional Teacher Digital Competence Scale. Descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, one-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlation, and simple linear regression were used. Overall digital competence was high. Scores did not differ significantly by gender, age, year of study, previous digital technology training, or previous AI training. Participants with digital material development experience had significantly higher competence (Hedges’ g = 0.76). Self-assessed AI use competence was strongly and positively associated with overall digital competence (r = .646) and accounted for 41.7% of its variance. The findings suggest that active digital production and AI-supported material development experiences are associated with stronger digital competence and deserve attention in teacher education.

items.title: Digital Entrepreneurship and High Performance in Jordanian Financial Services: Evidence from PLS-SEM and Implications for Organizational Learning
items.abstract: This study investigates how digital entrepreneurship drives high performance in Jordanian financial services companies and clarifies the human and organizational learning mechanisms behind this link. Survey data from 221 managers across 27 firms (proportional stratified sampling) measured five dimensions of digital entrepreneurship (digital leadership, knowledge, finance, culture, innovation) and four dimensions of high performance (continuous improvement, workforce quality, teamwork, flexible work systems). Descriptive statistics (SPSS) and PLS-SEM revealed a significant positive effect of digital entrepreneurship on high performance, with digital leadership, digital culture, and digital innovation emerging as the strongest predictors. Findings position digital transformation as a capability-building process: firms that institutionalize continuous digital upskilling, codify knowledge-sharing routines, align leadership and culture with innovation governance, and invest in FinTech-enabled processes and data capabilities achieve more robust high-performance work systems. The study contributes applied insights for educational studies and the applied humanities by framing digital entrepreneurship as a learning organization endeavor—where human-centered change, workforce development, and collaborative practices translate technology adoption into sustained performance. Practically, managers should embed structured learning pathways, cross-functional teamwork, and flexible work design to accelerate improvement. Sector-specific evidence from an emerging economy extends the literature and offers actionable guidance for policy and practice in digitally evolving financial services.

items.title: Digital Learning and Social Inclusion: Exploring Educational Equity in the 21st Century
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital technologies has fundamentally transformed how education is delivered, accessed, and experienced across the globe. This paper examines the relationship between digital learning and social inclusion, exploring whether technology-mediated education advances or undermines equity in the twenty-first century. Drawing on a review of literature published between 2019 and 2026, the study investigates how digital tools, ranging from remote learning platforms to artificial intelligence-driven personalization systems, shape access to quality education for historically marginalized groups, including low-income students, learners with disabilities, rural populations, and linguistic minorities. The paper adopts a qualitative, desk-based research methodology, synthesizing peer-reviewed studies, international policy reports, and systematic reviews to map the enabling conditions and persistent barriers associated with digital educational equity. Findings indicate that while digital learning holds considerable potential to widen access, personalize instruction, and support diverse learners through assistive and adaptive technologies, this potential is unevenly realized due to persistent digital divides in infrastructure, device access, connectivity, and digital literacy. The analysis further reveals that artificial intelligence-enabled tools can both mitigate and exacerbate educational inequality depending on how thoughtfully they are designed, governed, and deployed. The paper concludes that achieving genuine educational equity in a digitally mediated era requires deliberate policy intervention, inclusive design principles, and sustained investment in infrastructure and teacher capacity, rather than reliance on technology diffusion alone. Recommendations include embedding equity audits into EdTech procurement, strengthening digital literacy programs for underserved communities, and prioritizing universal design for learning within national digital education strategies.

items.title: Digital technologies and mental health in young people in higher education
items.abstract: Abstract: Scientific literature has shown an association between the use of digital technologies and the mental health of higher education students. However, gaps remain regarding the digital practices used to promote mental health literacy. In this context, a qualitative study was conducted using six focus groups, involving 43 students from 32 courses at 18 Portuguese higher education institutions. Thematic analysis of the data identified five themes: Digital habits; Digital technologies in mentalhealth literacy; Impact of digital technologies on well-being and mental health; Evaluation of digital technologies in mental health; Good practices in promoting well-being and mental health. The results show that the focus groups provided spaces for critical reflection and collective construction of knowledge concerning the benefits, risks and limitations of digital technologies in mental health. However, a discrepancy was identified between the participants’ critical discourse and their actualpractices. Despite reservations about the use of non-specialist digital tools, there is widespread reliance on social media content and artificial intelligence. This finding highlights a focus on immediacy, anonymity and accessibility, underscoring the need to gain a better understanding of these mechanisms and to improve access to specialist services.

items.title: DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES AND STUDENT-CENTERED LEARNING IN MODERN HIGHER EDUCATION
items.abstract: The digital transformation of education has significantly changed approaches to teaching and learning in higher education. Traditional teacher-centered instruction is increasingly being supplemented by interactive, personalized, and student-centered learning models supported by digital technologies. This article examines the pedagogical potential of learning management systems, digital communication platforms, artificial intelligence tools, multimedia resources, virtual learning environments, and online assessment technologies. The study employs theoretical analysis and synthesis of contemporary educational research. The results suggest that digital technologies can strengthen students’ autonomy, collaboration, critical thinking, motivation, and access to educational resources when they are integrated according to clearly defined pedagogical objectives. At the same time, excessive dependence on technology, digital inequality, academic integrity problems, information overload, and insufficient digital competence among educators remain important challenges. The paper argues that the effectiveness of educational digitalization depends not on the quantity of technological tools but on their pedagogically appropriate application. Keywords: digital education, student-centered learning, higher education, educational technology, digital competence, active learning, pedagogy

items.title: Digital Transformation of Disaster Response in Wajima City Following the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake: Implementation Process and Operational Conditions —A Comparative Case Analysis of Five Operations—
items.abstract: This study examines the implementation process and operational conditions determining the success or failure of the digital transformation of disaster response in Wajima City, Ishikawa Prefecture, following the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake. The study is based on a single-case comparative analysis of five operations—post-earthquake building safety assessment, shelter management, temporary housing, facility management, and publicly funded demolition—using operational records, products, meeting materials, and development logs. These operations were compared using five dimensions: digitalization of information collection, accumulation of shareable data, situational awareness through visualization, connection to decision support, and cross-departmental coordination. Among the five operations, post-earthquake building safety assessment and temporary housing advanced most continuously, while shelter management and facility management tended to remain at the stage of visualization, and publicly funded demolition remained fragmented. The results reveal that the digital transformation of disaster response progressed step by step from data input to accumulation, visualization, and decision support, rather than emerging all at once. Self-contained operations tended to advance more smoothly, whereas cross-departmental operations required clearer coordination and decision-making mechanisms. Thus, success depended less on technology itself than on operational conditions, implying that effective implementation depends on the peacetime preparation of data items, identifiers, update responsibilities, and decision-making arrangements.

items.title: Digital Transformation of Municipal Corporations in India: Opportunities and Challenges for Achieving the Viksit Bharat 2047 Vision
items.abstract: Abstract India’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 seeks to transform the country into a developed nation by the centenary of independence. Municipal corporations have a central role in this transformation because the quality of urban governance directly affects citizens’ everyday lives, economic activity, environmental sustainability and social well-being. Rapid urbanisation, increasing demand for public services, climate-related risks and growing expectations for transparent administration have created a need for municipal institutions to adopt digital technologies. This paper examines the opportunities and challenges associated with the digital transformation of municipal corporations in India. It explores how technologies such as artificial intelligence, geographic information systems, cloud computing, digital payment systems, data analytics, Internet of Things applications and online citizen-service platforms can improve municipal administration. Particular attention is given to digital revenue collection, solid-waste management, water and sanitation services, urban planning, grievance redressal, traffic management and citizen participation. The paper argues that digital transformation should not be understood merely as the computerisation of existing municipal processes. Instead, it should involve institutional reform, data-driven decision-making, inclusive service delivery, employee capacity building, cybersecurity and sustainable urban development. At the same time, municipalities face challenges including inadequate digital infrastructure, financial constraints, shortage of skilled personnel, fragmented databases, cybersecurity risks, unequal access to technology and resistance to organisational change. The paper proposes a citizen-centric and sustainable digital governance framework through which municipal corporations can contribute meaningfully to the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision.

items.title: Digital Transformation of Municipal Corporations in India: Opportunities and Challenges for Achieving the Viksit Bharat 2047 Vision
items.abstract: Abstract India’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 seeks to transform the country into a developed nation by the centenary of independence. Municipal corporations have a central role in this transformation because the quality of urban governance directly affects citizens’ everyday lives, economic activity, environmental sustainability and social well-being. Rapid urbanisation, increasing demand for public services, climate-related risks and growing expectations for transparent administration have created a need for municipal institutions to adopt digital technologies. This paper examines the opportunities and challenges associated with the digital transformation of municipal corporations in India. It explores how technologies such as artificial intelligence, geographic information systems, cloud computing, digital payment systems, data analytics, Internet of Things applications and online citizen-service platforms can improve municipal administration. Particular attention is given to digital revenue collection, solid-waste management, water and sanitation services, urban planning, grievance redressal, traffic management and citizen participation. The paper argues that digital transformation should not be understood merely as the computerisation of existing municipal processes. Instead, it should involve institutional reform, data-driven decision-making, inclusive service delivery, employee capacity building, cybersecurity and sustainable urban development. At the same time, municipalities face challenges including inadequate digital infrastructure, financial constraints, shortage of skilled personnel, fragmented databases, cybersecurity risks, unequal access to technology and resistance to organisational change. The paper proposes a citizen-centric and sustainable digital governance framework through which municipal corporations can contribute meaningfully to the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision.

items.title: Digital Transformation of Teacher Education under Vikshit Bharat @2047
items.abstract: Abstract India's vision of Vikshit Bharat @2047 rests on building a digitally empowered, innovation-driven, and sustainable economy in which artificial intelligence, e-commerce, and digital infrastructure serve as engines of inclusive growth. Realising this vision depends critically on the quality of human capital that education systems produce, and teacher education stands at the centre of that pipeline. This paper examines how the digital transformation envisaged under Vikshit Bharat @2047 is reshaping teacher education in India, using the reforms introduced under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 as the entry point. It discusses how national digital platforms such as DIKSHA, SWAYAM, and PM eVIDYA, together with emerging technologies including artificial intelligence, virtual and augmented reality, blockchain, and the Internet of Things, are creating new possibilities for personalised, inclusive, and lifelong teacher development. The paper also situates these developments within the wider digital economy, arguing that a technologically competent teaching workforce is a precondition for the commerce, innovation, and productivity gains that Vikshit Bharat @2047 anticipates. At the same time, the paper identifies significant risks, including the digital divide, uneven digital literacy among teachers, and adverse effects of excessive technology use on mental well-being, sleep, and attention. Drawing on secondary literature and policy documents, the paper proposes a blended and sustainability-oriented framework for teacher education that combines digital tools with face-to-face mentoring, structured digital wellness training, and continuous monitoring of technology use. It concludes that India's digital future will be strongest where digital ambition is matched with digital responsibility, and where teacher education is treated as strategic national infrastructure rather than a peripheral concern.

items.title: Digital Twin: Surgical Rehearsal Platform
items.abstract: Digital Twin technology has emerged as a transformative approach in modern healthcare by enabling the creation of patient-specific virtual replicas that accurately represent anatomical structures and physiological behavior. This paper proposes an Artificial Intelligence based Digital Twin framework for surgical rehearsal and preoperative planning that integrates medical imaging, three-dimensional reconstruction, and predictive AI models to assist surgeons in evaluating surgical strategies before entering the operating room. The proposed framework utilizes Computed Tomography and Magnetic Resonance Imaging scans to generate a personalized three-dimensional digital model of the patient's organ. Artificial Intelligence techniques are employed for image segmentation, anatomical structure identification, risk prediction, and simulation analysis. Surgeons can interact with the virtual model to perform multiple rehearsal scenarios, evaluate different surgical approaches, and estimate possible complications before the actual procedure. The framework aims to reduce surgical uncertainty, improve procedural accuracy, minimize intraoperative risks, and support informed clinical decision making. In addition, the proposed system offers educational benefits by providing a realistic training environment for medical students and surgical residents without exposing patients to unnecessary risks. The architecture is designed to be scalable and can be extended to multiple medical specialties, including cardiac surgery, neurosurgery, orthopedic surgery, and organ transplantation. By combining Artificial Intelligence with Digital Twin technology, the proposed framework demonstrates significant potential to enhance surgical precision, improve patient safety, optimize healthcare resources, and advance the future of personalized medicine.

items.title: Does Learning Protein Folding Generalize to Broader Reasoning?
items.abstract: Large language models rely heavily on human text, which often conveys surface answers rather than the spatial and structural logic behind them. Protein folding is a natural testbed, because one solved structure yields thousands of exactly checkable spatial and topological statements. We ask: can learning to fold proteins teach general models reusable reasoning capabilities? To answer this, we build FoldingCorpus, a protein-derived question-answer dataset, and Fold2Reason, a recipe that post-trains on it through two complementary signals: discrete structural answers predicted via the model's native language head, and continuous 3D geometry decoded from the same shared representations. On FoldBench, Fold2Reason achieves structure prediction scores 2.7 to 3.5 times those of Qwen3.5-9B. Beyond protein structure prediction, it improves performance on all 10 benchmarks spanning spatial, graph, scientific, and general reasoning, raising macro-average accuracy from 45.09% to 48.33% (+3.23 pp), with positive gains on all 10 benchmarks, while matched controls built from random, synthetic, and shuffled structure yield substantially smaller or negative gains. Our work shows that non-linguistic, structure-dense scientific data can systematically improve broad reasoning in language models, making a solved scientific problem a practical source of post-training supervision.

items.title: Does the Front Row Carry It All? Concrete Edge Failure of Multi-Row Anchor Groups in EN 1992-4—A Critical Re-Examination by Hand Calculation, Nonlinear Finite-Element Analysis (Code_Aster) and the AAS Equal-Share Method
items.abstract: EN 1992-4 verifies concrete edge failure of a multi-row anchor group loaded in shear towards a free edge by assuming that only the row closest to the edge is effective and that it carries the whole shear load. The consequence is paradoxical: the verified resistance does not grow when rows are added behind the front row, it falls when a row is added in front of existing anchors, and it rises when the holes of the front row are deliberately slotted so that those anchors carry nothing. For a 3 × 3 group of M12 wedge anchors (s = 150 mm, hef = 70 mm, C25/30, h = 250 mm) at c1 = 75, 100 and 150 mm, the code gives 31, 39 and 56 kN (uncracked), while the same anchors with the front row slotted give 73, 78 and 87 kN. The paper examines this rule with three tools: the EN 1992-4 calculation, the equal-share method implemented in the AAS anchor-design software (every anchor carries the same share and the front row is verified with its share only), and a three-dimensional nonlinear finite-element analysis in Code_Aster with a regularised damage model for concrete, elastic steel shanks and a rigid fixture. The analyses show that, without hole clearance, every row is active up to failure: at peak load the front row carries practically its own stand-alone resistance while the two rows behind it carry 2.1 to 4.4 times as much, and the group resists 5.4, 3.9 and 2.9 times the load of the front row acting alone — where EN 1992-4 assumes 1.0. Removing the front row altogether does not increase the computed resistance, so adding anchors near the edge does not weaken the group, and with a hole clearance that lets the front row fail first the group still reaches 92 to 94 % of its resistance, at a larger displacement. Normalised to the characteristic level, the finite-element group resistance is about 147, 146 and 161 kN, i.e. 4.7, 3.8 and 2.9 times the EN value. The equal-share (AAS) method is close to this behaviour and conservative for c1 = 75 and 100 mm, but at c1 = 150 mm it reaches the resistance of the global break-out body that starts behind the back row, which the equal-share rule does not see. A verification rule is therefore proposed that keeps the equal share and adds that global check: the group resistance is the lesser of (n/n1) times the front-row resistance and the resistance of the back row carrying the whole load. For the cases studied it is conservative by a nearly constant factor of 1.4 to 1.6 with respect to the normalised finite-element results, against 2.9 to 4.7 for the present rule. Evaluated with the ACI 318-19 break-out equations, the same two checks — which correspond to cases illustrated in the ACI commentary — give 94, 124 and 147 kN, and a worked design example in cracked concrete shows the practical consequence: a fixture that fails the EN check by a factor of two passes the proposed one with a utilisation of 0.8.

items.title: DPMF: A Dynamic Risk-Aware Permission Framework for Securing AI Agents Using Third-Party APIs
items.abstract: AI agents are moving from systems that only generate information to systems that can plan tasks, use tools, and perform operations through external APIs. This shift creates a security problem that traditional permission models do not fully address: an agent may hold broad privileges even when a particular task needs only a small part of that access. A valid token therefore does not automatically mean that every action produced by the agent is appropriate. This paper proposes DPMF (Dynamic Risk-Aware Permission Framework), an external authorization layer for AI agents that interact with third-party services. DPMF evaluates each proposed API action using contextual signals such as user-intent alignment, data sensitivity, permission severity, source trust, action reversibility, and behavioral deviation. The resulting risk level drives one of four decisions: Allow, Restrict, Human Approval, or Deny. The framework also separates the agent's ability to propose an action from the security layer's authority to approve it. The paper presents the framework architecture, threat model, risk-scoring approach, dynamic permission algorithm, case study, and an experimental methodology for comparing DPMF with static authorization. Because the framework has not yet been experimentally implemented, no numerical performance claims are presented as established results. Instead, measurable evaluation criteria and expected outcomes are defined.

items.title: Drift Inspector: Exploring and Measuring Scientific Drift with Atomic Contribution Claims
items.abstract: Scientific abstracts mix contributions with background, motivation, and meta-language, so tools that read them as-is cannot separate what a field produces from what it discusses. We present Drift Inspector, an open-source system for measuring and exploring how a research field changes over time at the level of Atomic Contribution Claims (ACCs): decontextualized, contribution-bearing propositions an LLM extracts from each abstract before analysis. The system clusters these claims across years into an interactive map where every trend traces back to the claims and papers behind it. Applied to six years of EMNLP, it shows the field shifting away from classic NLP tasks toward LLM-era capabilities such as reasoning and multimodality -- a movement that keyword or whole-abstract counts blur. The released data extend beyond EMNLP: the same pipeline has processed the full ACL Anthology (346k claims, 80k abstracts, 423 venues). Extraction is human-validated and clustering checked against an external manually constructed taxonomy.

items.title: Driving the future: Evaluating a training concept for advanced driver assistance systems
items.abstract: With the widespread adoption of Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS), the need for effective ADAS driver training increases. However, empirical evidence regarding the effectiveness of ADAS education remains limited. This study evaluated the effectiveness of an ADAS driver training program across four European countries. The training included classroom-based theoretical instruction and practical hands-on experience on test-tracks and open-roads. 166 participants completed a questionnaire measuring their knowledge, attitudes, and behavioral intentions towards ADAS pre- and post-training. Overall knowledge of system purpose, handling and limitations improved significantly with the training. However, some misunderstandings remained, and in some cases, misconceptions from before the training were not corrected. Perceived safety and trust remained unchanged while willingness to use ADAS systems, and the perceived ease of use and usefulness of ADAS increased. Future training should not only provide information for trainees but also identify misconceptions they may hold. Follow-up or feedback sessions are recommended to address potential misunderstandings.

items.title: E-Tactile Flow: Exploring A Novel Path of Pain Relief through Interactive Electrotactile Stimulation
items.abstract: Chronic or recurrent pain significantly impairs quality of life, and conventional pharmacological treatments often produce side effects, motivating the search for non-pharmacological alternatives. This study introduces a novel paradigm — E-Tactile Tactile Flow (E-Tactile Flow)—which integrates electrotactile stimulation with attentional engagement and flow-related task design. Inspired by a bidirectional attention mechanism, the paradigm designed goal-directed task mode and stimulus-driven task mode to examine the role of cognitive engagement in pain modulation. A preliminary study validated the feasibility and safety parameters of an 8×8 electrotactile system. In Experiment 1 (n = 42), both attention modes effectively reduced pain perception, with the goal-directed task mode showing significantly stronger modulation of several physiological measures and a marginal trend toward lower subjective pain ratings than the stimulus-driven task mode. Building on this, Experiment 2 introduced adaptive difficulty modulation to better align task challenge with participant performance. Results showed that dynamic task adjustment significantly enhanced attentional engagement and reduced pain ratings. Overall, this study provides initial empirical support for an electrotactile interaction paradigm for non-pharmacological pain modulation.

items.title: EcoPro-LSTMv0: A Memory-based Machine Learning Approach to Predicting Ecosystem Dynamics across Time Scales in Mediterranean Environments
items.abstract: EcoPro-LSTM is version 0 of Ecosystem Process Modelling using a Long Short-Term Memory Approach. The model uses a Multi-Task Multi-Timescale Long Short-Term Memory (MT-LSTM) modelling framework. EcoPro-LSTM was developed by Mitra Cattry et al. as part of the research “EcoPro-LSTM v0: A Memory-based Machine Learning Approach to Predicting Ecosystem Dynamics across Time Scales in Mediterranean Environments,” accepted for publication in Machine Learning: Earth (2026). The work was financially supported by the Swiss National Science Foundation, Award #P500PN_206603, and the National Science Foundation (NSF) Science and Technology Center (STC) Learning the Earth with Artificial Intelligence and Physics (LEAP), Award #2019625-STC. The model predicts environmental variables including gross primary productivity (carbon uptake), ecosystem respiration, evapotranspiration, and surface soil moisture across multiple timescales using a single LSTM architecture, as described in the accompanying tutorial. Integrated gradients are used to enhance model interpretability by identifying the influence of climatic drivers such as precipitation. For questions, issues, or further assistance with the code, please contact Mitra Cattry at mitra.cattry@gmail.com.
